subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: \(\triangle DEF \sim \triangle MNK\). If \(DE = 5\) and \(MN = 6\), then find the value of \(\dfrac{A(\triangle DEF)}{A(\triangle MNK)}\).
solution:
The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.
\(\dfrac{A(\triangle DEF)}{A(\triangle MNK)} = \dfrac{DE^2}{MN^2} = \dfrac{5^2}{6^2} = \dfrac{25}{36}\).

stem: If two circles with radii \(8\) cm and \(3\) cm respectively touch externally, then find the distance between their centres.
solution:
Let \(r_1 = 8\) cm and \(r_2 = 3\) cm. When two circles touch externally, the distance between their centres equals the sum of their radii.
Distance \(= r_1 + r_2 = 8 + 3 = 11\) cm.

stem: Find the length of the altitude of an equilateral triangle with side \(6\) cm.
solution:
Let \(\triangle ABC\) be equilateral with side \(6\) cm and \(AD\) its altitude, so \(\triangle ADC\) is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) triangle with \(\angle ACD = 60^\circ\).
\(AD = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times AB = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 6 = 3\sqrt{3}\) cm.
Hence the altitude is \(3\sqrt{3}\) cm.

stem: If \(\theta = 45^\circ\), then find \(\tan\theta\).
Slope of a line is \(3\) and \(y\)-intercept is \(-4\). Write the equation of the line.
solution:
Slope \(m = 3\) and \(y\)-intercept \(c = -4\). The equation of a line is \(y = mx + c\).
\(\therefore y = 3x - 4\).

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: The ratio of the areas of two triangles with the common base is \(10 : 7\). Height of the larger triangle is \(15\) cm, then find the corresponding height of the smaller triangle.
solution:
For triangles with a common base, the ratio of areas equals the ratio of their heights.
Let the heights be \(h_1 = 15\) cm (larger) and \(h_2\) (smaller).
\(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \dfrac{h_1}{h_2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{10}{7} = \dfrac{15}{h_2}\)
\(h_2 = \dfrac{15 \times 7}{10} = 10.5\) cm.

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: In the following figure, point \(A\) is the centre of the circle. Line \(MN\) is tangent at point \(M\). If \(AN = 16\) cm and \(MN = 8\) cm, determine the radius of the circle.
solution:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so \(AM \perp MN\) and \(\triangle AMN\) is right-angled at \(M\).
By the Pythagoras theorem, \(AM^2 + MN^2 = AN^2\).
\(AM^2 + 8^2 = 16^2\)
\(AM^2 = 256 - 64 = 192\)
\(AM = \sqrt{192} = \sqrt{64 \times 3} = 8\sqrt{3}\) cm.
Hence the radius of the circle is \(8\sqrt{3}\) cm.
figureNote: circle with centre A; tangent line MN touching at M with N on the line outside; segments AM (radius) and AN drawn, p-00

stem: Draw \(\angle XYZ\) of measure \(50^\circ\) and bisect it.
solution:
Steps of construction:
1) Draw \(\angle XYZ = 50^\circ\).
2) With the compass point on \(Y\) and a convenient radius, draw an arc cutting rays \(YX\) and \(YZ\) at \(S\) and \(P\) respectively.
3) With the same radius, draw arcs from \(S\) and from \(P\) inside the angle so that they cut each other at \(T\).
4) Draw ray \(YT\). Ray \(YT\) is the bisector of \(\angle XYZ\) (each part measures \(25^\circ\)).

stem: If \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{24}{25}\), where \(\theta\) is an acute angle, find the value of \(\sin\theta\).
solution:
Using \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\):
\(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \left(\dfrac{24}{25}\right)^2 = 1 - \dfrac{576}{625} = \dfrac{49}{625}\)
\(\sin\theta = \pm\dfrac{7}{25}\). Since \(\theta\) is acute, \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{7}{25}\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: The volume of a cube is \(216\) cm\(^3\). Find its side.
solution:
Let \(x\) be the side of the cube. Then \(x^3 = 216 = 6^3\), so \(x = 6\) cm.
Hence the side of the cube is \(6\) cm.

stem: The radius and slant height of a cone are \(10\) cm and \(30\) cm respectively. Find the curved surface area of that cone. \((\pi = 3.14)\)
solution: Curved surface area of a cone \(= \pi r l = 3.14 \times 10 \times 30 = 942\) cm\(^2\).

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
context: In the following figure, seg \(DH \perp\) seg \(EF\) and seg \(GK \perp\) seg \(EF\). If \(DH = 12\) cm, \(GK = 20\) cm and \(A(\triangle DEF) = 300\) cm\(^2\), then find the following.
stem: Find \(EF\).
solution:
\(A(\triangle DEF) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times EF \times DH\)
\(300 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times EF \times 12\)
\(EF = \dfrac{300 \times 2}{12} = 50\) cm.

stem: In the following figure, ray \(PA\) is tangent to the circle at \(A\) and \(PBC\) is a secant. If \(AP = 18\), \(BP = 10\), then find \(BC\).
solution:
By the tangent-secant segments property, \(BP \times PC = AP^2\).
\(10 \times PC = 18^2 = 324\)
\(PC = 32.4\)
\(BC = PC - BP = 32.4 - 10 = 22.4\) units.
figureNote: circle with tangent ray PA touching at A and secant through P meeting the circle at B then C; external point P, p-01

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw the circle with centre \(C\) and radius \(3.3\) cm. Take a point \(B\) at a distance \(6.6\) cm from the centre \(C\). Draw tangents to the circle from the point \(B\).
solution:
Steps of construction:
1) Construct a circle with centre \(C\) and radius \(3.3\) cm.
2) Take a point \(B\) such that \(CB = 6.6\) cm.
3) Obtain the midpoint \(M\) of seg \(CB\).
4) Draw a circle with centre \(M\) and radius \(MB\).
5) Let \(S\) and \(T\) be the points of intersection of these two circles.
6) Draw lines \(BS\) and \(BT\); these are the required tangents.

stem: Show that \(\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 + \cos A}} = \operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 + \cos A}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 + \cos A} \times \dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 - \cos A}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(1 - \cos A)^2}{1 - \cos^2 A}}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{(1 - \cos A)^2}{\sin^2 A}} = \dfrac{1 - \cos A}{\sin A} = \dfrac{1}{\sin A} - \dfrac{\cos A}{\sin A} = \operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A = \) R.H.S.

stem: Write the equation of the line passing through \(A(-2, -3)\) and \(B(-4, 7)\) in the form \(ax + by + c = 0\).
Prove that, "the lengths of the two tangent segments to a circle drawn from an external point are equal".
solution:
Given: A circle with centre \(O\), an external point \(P\), and two tangents from \(P\) touching the circle at \(A\) and \(B\).
To prove: \(PA = PB\).
Construction: Draw seg \(OA\), seg \(OB\) and seg \(OP\).
Proof: \(\angle PAO = \angle PBO = 90^\circ\) (tangent is perpendicular to the radius).
In right-angled triangles \(PAO\) and \(PBO\):
seg \(OA =\) seg \(OB\) (radii of the same circle),
hypotenuse \(PO =\) hypotenuse \(PO\) (common).
\(\therefore \triangle PAO \cong \triangle PBO\) (hypotenuse-side test)
\(\Rightarrow PA = PB\) (corresponding sides of congruent triangles).

stem: A tree is broken by the wind. The top of that tree struck the ground at an angle of \(30^\circ\) and at a distance of \(30\) m from the root. Find the height of the whole tree. \((\sqrt{3} = 1.73)\)
solution:
Let \(AB\) be the unbroken part standing at the root \(B\), and the broken part \(AC\) reaches the ground at \(C\), with \(BC = 30\) m and \(\angle ACB = 30^\circ\). The broken part \(AC\) equals the fallen top \(AT\), so total height \(= AB + AT\).
In right \(\triangle ABC\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BC} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{AB}{30} \Rightarrow AB = \dfrac{30}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.
Also \(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{BC}{AC} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{30}{AC} \Rightarrow AC = \dfrac{60}{\sqrt{3}}\) m, so \(AT = \dfrac{60}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.
Height \(= AB + AT = \dfrac{30}{\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{60}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{90}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{90\sqrt{3}}{3} = 30\sqrt{3} = 30 \times 1.73 = 51.90\) m.

stem: \(A(5, 4)\), \(B(-3, -2)\) and \(C(1, -8)\) are the vertices of triangle \(ABC\). Find the equation of median \(AD\).
solution:
\(AD\) is the median, so \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\).
\(x\)-coordinate of \(D = \dfrac{-3 + 1}{2} = -1\); \(y\)-coordinate of \(D = \dfrac{-2 + (-8)}{2} = -5\). So \(D(-1, -5)\).
Slope of \(AD = \dfrac{-5 - 4}{-1 - 5} = \dfrac{-9}{-6} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).
Equation: \(y - 4 = \dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)\)
\(2y - 8 = 3x - 15\)
\(2y - 3x + 7 = 0\).

stem: Prove that, in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the remaining two sides.
solution:
Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\).
To prove: \(AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2\).
Construction: Draw seg \(BD \perp\) hypotenuse \(AC\), \(A\text{-}D\text{-}C\).
Proof: In \(\triangle ABC\), seg \(BD \perp\) hypotenuse \(AC\), so \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADB\) (similarity in right-angled triangles).
\(\dfrac{AB}{AD} = \dfrac{AC}{AB} \Rightarrow AB^2 = AC \times AD\) ...(i)
Similarly \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle BDC\), so \(\dfrac{BC}{DC} = \dfrac{AC}{BC} \Rightarrow BC^2 = AC \times DC\) ...(ii)
Adding (i) and (ii): \(AB^2 + BC^2 = AC \times AD + AC \times DC = AC(AD + DC) = AC \times AC = AC^2\).
\(\therefore AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2\).

stem: \(\triangle SHR \sim \triangle SVU\). In \(\triangle SHR\), \(SH = 4.5\) cm, \(HR = 5.2\) cm, \(SR = 5.8\) cm and \(\dfrac{SH}{SV} = \dfrac{3}{5}\). Construct \(\triangle SVU\).
solution:
Steps of construction:
1) Draw \(\triangle SHR\) with \(SH = 4.5\) cm, \(HR = 5.2\) cm and \(SR = 5.8\) cm.
2) Construct an acute \(\angle HSZ\) at \(S\) on the side of \(SH\) opposite to vertex \(R\).
3) Mark off five points (the greater of \(3\) and \(5\) in \(\dfrac{3}{5}\)) \(S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4, S_5\) on ray \(SZ\) such that \(HS_1 = S_1S_2 = S_2S_3 = S_3S_4 = S_4S_5\).
4) Join \(S_3\) to \(H\) and draw a line \(S_5V\) parallel to \(S_3H\), intersecting the extended \(SH\) at \(V\).
5) Draw a line through \(V\) parallel to \(HR\) intersecting the extended segment \(SR\) at \(U\).
Thus, \(\triangle SVU\) is the required triangle.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: If \(V\) is the volume of a cuboid of dimensions \(a \times b \times c\) and \(S\) is its surface area, then prove that \(\dfrac{1}{V} = \dfrac{2}{S}\left(\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c}\right)\).
solution:
Volume \(V = a \times b \times c\) and surface area \(S = 2(ab + bc + ca)\).
\(\dfrac{2}{S}\left(\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c}\right) = \dfrac{2}{2(ab + bc + ca)}\left(\dfrac{bc + ca + ab}{abc}\right) = \dfrac{1}{abc} = \dfrac{1}{V}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{1}{V} = \dfrac{2}{S}\left(\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c}\right)\).
